acts.desc: Host Ira Glass explains that this hour we will hear from people from all over the country, with different points of view, explain what they’re feeling and thinking about Donald Trump’s election.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: Two police officers who voted for Obama in 2008 explain to Producer Miki Meek why they went for Trump this time around.
acts.title: South Florida

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
Producer Neil Drumming talks to someone who was not happy with the results of Tuesday’s
election. Janelle, who’s black, is bracing herself for the coming days.
acts.title: Metro-North Train

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Producer Karen Duffin visits someone who actually knows the man who’s going to be President: Donald Trump’s neighbor.
acts.title: Trump Tower

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Producer Jonathan Menjivar listens in on parent-teacher conferences the day after the election at a bilingual school in Los Angeles.
acts.title: Los Angeles

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc:
For some people, this election wasn’t just about choosing a politician. It was about choosing
their new boss. Producer Stephanie Foo hangs out with two Army Reservists who have very
different opinions about their new Commander-in-Chief.
acts.title: Long Island

acts.label: Act Six
acts.desc: Ira talks to a Muslim woman who tweeted on election night that she was worried she would no longer feel safe wearing a hijab.
acts.title: Times Square

acts.label: Act Seven
acts.desc:
Donald Trump has promised to get rid of Obamacare. Producer David Kestenbaum talks with
someone who’d lose their insurance.
acts.title: Nicholasville, Kentucky

acts.label: Act Eight
acts.desc:
We’ve been talking to Trump voters all year—a time during which they’ve watched their
candidate’s chances evolve from laughable, to likely, to striking distance, to victory. Producer Zoe Chace checks in with a father and son who’ve been Trump supporters since February, when their guy was an underdog.
acts.title: Greenville South Carolina

acts.label: Act Nine
acts.desc: Elna Baker talks to a Republican woman who voted for Hillary Clinton this year, and has suffered consequences in the Mormon community she lives in.
acts.title: Salt Lake City

acts.label: Act Ten
acts.desc: Producer Zoe Chace hung out with some immigration lawyers who are getting calls from their nervous clients.
acts.title: New York City

acts.label: Act Eleven
acts.desc: On election night, producer Emmanuel Dzotsi was the last person at our office. Just before midnight, he got on the phone to his mom in Ohio, and recorded their conversation.
acts.title: Toledo
